prompt: Which creates a thread that prints 'Hello' and starts it correctly?
choices: Thread t = new Thread(); t.run(); // prints Hello
Thread t = new Thread(() -> System.out.println("Hello")); t.start();
explanation: Pass a Runnable lambda to the Thread constructor and call start() (not run()). Calling run() directly executes on the current thread — no new thread is created. Option C: Thread.run() is not a static method. Option D: Runnable has no start() method.
